cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID
The verifier skips coverage (the project has no coverage script), so no run reports coverage.
Its own database, so no other test's state moves these counts.
one Scheduled appointment started on 1 August 2026 (outside Last 30 days)
if (startsAt.getTime() <= this.clock().getTime()) throw fieldError('startsAt', 'must be in the future');
Given a counted appointment belongs to a patient with a phone number and email recorded
REQ-10, REQ-11: neither the dashboard nor the tile's list contains contact details or medical history (S-4).

findings.suggested_fix: Give a counted patient an email in the test setup, then assert that the phone and email values, as well as the key names, are absent from the dashboard and list JSON.
findings.text: S-4 AC5 needs a counted patient with a phone and an email recorded, but the fixture patients have no email. The REQ-11 check only searches the JSON for the key names phone/email, so an email value leaking under another key would go unnoticed.

rubric_items.reason: Every changed path has a test: the awaitingOutcome count, started=true on the list, the tile and its link, and AppointmentsPage passing started through. S-2 AC1 is now tested with the 1 August appointment, and S-1 AC5 and S-3 AC3 now have tests.

Assertions check exact counts, ordered ids, totals, hrefs, 400 field errors and labels limited to .tiles a.tile. The privacy check is weaker: it matches key names with a regex, and no fixture patient has an email recorded.

Edges covered: a start exactly at now, a 10:30 start not yet reached, the next day, a count of 0 with an empty list, an empty started= value, and dropping the count after completion. The error path covers started=false/yes/1 as a 400. The dashboard's 400 is already tested.

Uses Vitest and Supertest with its own PostgreSQL and a fixed clock, and Vitest with jsdom on the web side. Every new test name starts with HMS-21 and its REQ id, and the files sit in the existing test folders.

Pass/fail is left to checks.json, which shows build and test passing. Coverage is not claimed, which matches the verifier skipping coverage (exit 78). The per-file test counts match the files (12, 4 added, 2).
